prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move Sign-In After Pet Adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +13.3% (p=0.0), won
- round 1: Interactive Desktop Waiting Room [home, redesign]: predicted +8.0%, measured +5.6% (p=0.005388), won
- round 1: Photo Quality Guide & Companion Preview [adoption, incentive]: predicted +10.0%, measured +7.6% (p=0.00564), won

Previous lessons:
(none yet)

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Reordering sign-in until after pet adoption was effective and slightly outperformed predictions (+13.3% measured vs +12.0% predicted).
Home page redesigns like interactive waiting rooms are helpful (+5.6% measured), though initial predictions were too high (+8.0% predicted).
Adoption incentives like photo quality guides and companion previews improved results (+7.6% measured), but were overestimated (+10.0% predicted).
